healthcare_exposure.honest_assessment: Mixed value, and it should be described precisely rather than inflated. MOST of the duties are administrative — faxing, scanning, stamping, document runs — and those are not worth supp-app space; every applicant who has been near a clinic has done them. The part that matters is TAKING VITALS: height, weight, BP, temperature is direct, hands-on patient contact and a real clinical skill, and it is what distinguishes this from an office-admin placement. Rooming patients also puts him in the room with people who are anxious or unwell, which is the observational content worth writing about. Frame the placement around vitals and patient contact; mention the administrative work only if he can say something interesting about it (see below).
healthcare_exposure.correction_note: This does NOT close the sustained-clinical-commitment gap, contrary to the initial 2026-08-03 assessment made before these details were known. It ends August 13 and does not continue into the school year, which places it in the same category as the 30-hour Misericordia block: a good, genuine summer clinical experience, but episodic. McMaster's rubric rewards sustained commitment, and a six-week summer placement is not that. The gap is narrower than it was, not closed.
urgent_actions_before_aug_13: ASK ABOUT RETURNING part-time during the school year — even one shift a month converts this from 'summer volunteering' into an ongoing commitment, which is worth substantially more on the supplementary application than the extra hours themselves

Request a reference or letter of support, and get contact details for whoever is willing to vouch — likely the clinic manager or the most senior MOA. Also ask whether any physician at the clinic observed him enough to speak to it

healthcare_exposure.supp_app_angle: The strongest available intellectual bridge: Justin's IB CS IA is about early detection of at-risk students from survey response patterns. A primary care clinic is precisely where early detection of adult health problems succeeds or fails — and he has now watched the administrative load that sits between a physician and their patients (the faxing and scanning he did IS that load). If he noticed anything real about how paperwork volume, appointment length, or intake process affects what a physician is able to catch, that is a genuinely distinctive observation and connects his technical work to clinical practice. That is a far better use of this experience than listing duties.

projects_contributed_to.project: Electrically-triggered debonding adhesive (Hongjian Zhang's PhD project)
projects_contributed_to.description: A gel that cures and hardens underwater, bonding metal surfaces. Passing current from cathode through gel to anode irreversibly weakens it, allowing detachment. Two live competing mechanistic hypotheses: (1) non-covalent gel-metal bonds break, with OH reverting to O at chain ends; (2) an electrochemical reaction roughens both surfaces, reducing effective contact area and therefore adhesion.
projects_contributed_to.justin_contribution: Ran the universal testing machine voltage series at 3, 5, 7 and 9 V. Result: adhesion force decreases exponentially with increasing voltage; at 9 V the metals fully detach. Understands and can explain why raw force is converted to stress (force ÷ bonded area, kPa) — to normalize out sample geometry so values are comparable across samples and voltages.
projects_contributed_to.significance: This is his single best research artifact — real data he generated himself that bears on an open mechanistic question in a PhD project.

projects_contributed_to.description: A sialic acid / glycerol cosmetic product. Two problems being solved: sialic acid has an anti-viscous property so viscosity must be raised, and the product oxidizes and yellows.
projects_contributed_to.justin_contribution: Prepared the glycerol/water concentration series (2%, 5%, 10%) and ran Zetasizer particle-size and zeta-potential characterization to identify concentrations compatible with the instrument, which does not tolerate high concentration. research_experience.concepts_demonstrably_understood: DLVO theory and colloidal stability; the balance of van der Waals attraction against electrostatic double-layer repulsion; the primary minimum and the energy barrier; zeta potential correctly understood as a PROXY measured at the slipping plane rather than the repulsion itself; Brownian motion; DLS and PDI interpretation; viscoelasticity, storage vs loss modulus and the physical meaning of their crossover; Newtonian vs shear-thinning vs shear-thickening behaviour; stress normalization. The notes show genuine comprehension rather than copied definitions — the zeta-potential-as-proxy distinction and the force-to-stress reasoning are both the kind of thing a student only writes down once they have understood why.

research_experience.why_it_matters: This closes the single largest gap in the profile, and the detail confirms it is substantive rather than decorative. The May 23 report flagged formal lab-research experience as the visible weakness after HYRS was rejected — 'not fatal, but visible to McMaster and Queen's BHSc readers who know what a strong BHSc applicant looks like.' A paid position in a Tier 1 CRC lab is materially stronger than HYRS would have been: HYRS is a structured high-school summer program, this is a real research group hiring him. The 'paid' detail signals the lab valued the contribution enough to fund it rather than accommodate a student. Crucially, the journal shows he is OPERATING instruments and generating data by week two, not shadowing — the July 20 voltage series on Hongjian's project is his own data on an open mechanistic question.
research_experience.how_to_frame_for_bhsc: IMPORTANT AND EASY TO GET WRONG. This is soft-matter, colloid and interfacial science in a Chemical & Materials Engineering department — it is NOT clinical or biomedical research, and a BHSc reader will spot an overclaim instantly. Do not describe it as medical research. The honest and genuinely strong bridges are through BIOMATERIALS and DRUG DELIVERY, all of which are real and present in what he actually saw: chitosan/TPP nanoparticles (Tom's work, explicitly targeting antibacterial and antifungal clinical application, and a well-established drug-delivery vehicle); self-healing alginate/PAAM hydrogels (a major tissue-engineering and wound-dressing material class); sialic acid (a biologically central cell-surface sugar); and electrically-triggered debonding adhesives (an obvious application space in removable surgical and medical adhesives). Prof. Zeng's group lists biomedical engineering among its research areas. The accurate framing is: he worked on the physical chemistry that underlies biomaterials, and can explain why colloidal stability determines whether a drug-delivery particle works. That is more impressive than a vague claim to medical research, and it is true.

advanced_placement.summary: Two AP examinations, both scored 5/5 — Calculus BC and Biology. 5 is the top score on the AP scale.
advanced_placement.why_it_matters: Three distinct uses. (1) CORROBORATION: an externally validated 5 in Calculus BC independently confirms the math ability that his Alberta marks assert — Math 30-1 final 100%, Math 31 projected 100%. An out-of-province admissions reader who does not know Old Scona's grading culture can calibrate against a College Board score in a way they cannot against a school mark. Same function for AP Biology against his Biology 30 projection. (2) DE-RISKS MATH 31: he has already been examined at BC level, which covers material beyond Math 31, so the projected 100 in Math 31 is now a well-supported expectation rather than an optimistic one. This matters because Math 31 is one of the six top-6 courses. (3) POSSIBLE FIRST-YEAR CREDIT: most Canadian universities grant transfer credit or advanced standing for AP scores of 4 or 5, and a BC 5 commonly maps to first-year calculus. Worth checking each target program's AP transfer-credit policy once offers arrive — this is a practical benefit for first-year course load, not an admissions factor.
advanced_placement.admissions_caveat: AP scores are NOT an admission criterion at any of Justin's Ontario targets — admission runs on the Alberta top-6 average plus, where applicable, the supplementary application or AIF. AP results are supporting evidence and a credit-transfer opportunity, not a lever on the decision. Do not let AP work displace ELA 30-1 time.

McMaster requires 'formal individual assessment after accepting an admission offer.' Waterloo's Computer Science admission requirements for Alberta students list only Mathematics 30-1, Mathematics 31 and English Language Arts 30-1, with individual selection from the low-to-mid 90s, and make no reference to AP. Queen's admission pages do not present AP as satisfying any requirement (the sole AP mention is 'AP Calculus is recommended' for Smith Commerce). CONCLUSION: the AP scores do not raise Justin's admission average and are not needed to satisfy prerequisites, since his Alberta 30-level courses already cover every requirement. Their value is entirely post-admission credit, plus informal corroboration of ability.

transfer_credit_by_school.waterloo: Min score 4. AP Calculus BC → MATH 137 (0.5 units) for Faculty of Mathematics students, which INCLUDES Computer Science; MATH 127 (0.5 units) for everyone else. AP Biology → BIOL 239 + 130L (0.75 units). NOTE: the Faculty of Mathematics does not grant credit for AP Calculus AB or AP Statistics — only BC, which is what Justin has. BONUS: Math students with a grade of 5 may be eligible for advanced versions of some first-year courses. Maximum transfer credit varies by program (1.0-4.0 units). Official College Board results must reach Admissions by the deadline stated on the offer of admission. Credits may be declined.
transfer_credit_by_school.uoft: Min score 4. Maximum 3.0 credits total. IMPORTANT LIMIT: only 1.0 credit is granted per subject area, so multiple exams in one discipline do not stack. Same policy across Arts & Science (St. George), UTM and UTSC. The Faculty of Applied Science & Engineering grants no AP credit at all. Assessed after admission only.
transfer_credit_by_school.queens: Min score 4. Maximum 18.0 units. AP Calculus BC → MATH 121 (6.0 units). AP Biology → BIOL 102 + BIOL 103 (3.0 units each). CAUTIONS: MATH 121 credit excludes MATH 120, and MATH 120 is required for access to a Mathematics degree plan (irrelevant for BHSc, relevant if he ever switched). And if he later takes BIOL 102/103 at Queen's, those courses take precedence on the transcript and the AP credit stops counting toward the degree. Transfer credit must be requested by the end of the fall term of first year.
transfer_credit_by_school.mcmaster: Min score 4, up to 18 units, at the discretion of each Faculty. AP Calculus BC (4+) → MATH 1F03. AP Biology (4+) → 3 units of unspecified Level 1 Biology. Engineering I and iBioMed I may apply approved transfer credits only toward complementary studies electives. BHSc treatment not stated — confirm directly.
transfer_credit_by_school.western: Min score 4. Maximum 2.0 credits. For the BMSc program specifically, an AP transfer credit SATISFIES the minimum 60% first-year requirement in biology, chemistry, math or physics needed for progression. But if the student takes the Western course anyway, they FORFEIT the AP credit and must earn the minimum mark at Western. A math transfer credit must be equivalent to the 1.0 math course required by the intended Year-3 module, or first-year math must be taken at Western.
transfer_credit_by_school.ualberta: Min score 4. Transfer credit awarded either for a specific course or an unspecified 100-level course; no grade appears on the UAlberta transcript. NOTABLE: for prerequisite calculations and professional program admission, an AP grade of 5 is treated as 4.0 (A/A+) and a 4 as 3.7 (A-).

verified_2026_08_03.STRATEGIC_ADVICE_do_not_auto_accept: The default assumption should be to DECLINE the AP Biology credit and take first-year biology at university anyway. Justin is on a med-school track, and medical school admission is computed on university GPA. Skipping first-year biology removes a course he would very likely score highly in and pushes him into second-year material a year early, where the grade is harder and still counts. Acceleration is worth less than GPA protection for this specific path. The Queen's rule makes this explicit — take BIOL 102/103 there and the AP credit simply stops counting. Western's rule is the same in reverse: repeat the course and the credit is forfeited. The calculus credit is a closer call and depends on the program; at Waterloo the more interesting option is not the credit but eligibility for the ADVANCED first-year math stream, which is a genuine distinction. Decision point is after offers arrive (roughly May-August 2027), not now.
verified_2026_08_03.ACTION_TIMING: Nothing to do this fall. AP credit is irrelevant to the application itself. The one thing not to forget: official scores must be sent from the College Board directly to each university, and Waterloo ties this to the deadline stated on the offer of admission, while Queen's and McMaster require the request by the end of the fall term of first year.

technical_projects.name: Mental Health Risk Prediction Algorithm
technical_projects.status: COMPLETE, submitted to IB, and SHIPPED PUBLICLY (verified 2026-08-03).
technical_projects.description: Web-based survey platform and ML model to identify at-risk high school students from anonymized response patterns — targeting early intervention. The project Justin describes as 'the tool I wish had existed for my classmate.' Five-question screening returning a Low/Moderate/Elevated risk level plus Canadian crisis resources. Ensemble of LightGBM + XGBoost, Streamlit front end, trained on the Kaggle Playground Series S4E11 'Exploring Mental Health Data' dataset (~140,700 responses).

public_packaging_status.github_repo: https://github.com/chetocheese/CS-IA-student-mental-health-assessment — PUBLIC, verified 2026-08-03. README covers purpose, disclaimer, how it works, install instructions, and crisis resources. 3 commits on main.
public_packaging_status.note: Two of the three A3 pieces are done. Only the LinkedIn technical writeup remains.

technical_projects.STANDOUT_DETAIL: The tool is deployed on **helpingminds.ca — Justin's own non-profit's domain** — not on a generic free-tier host. This is materially stronger than a GitHub repo alone because it closes the narrative loop completely and verifiably: a grade-9 classmate's mental-health crisis → he founds HelpingMinds.ca → he teaches himself LightGBM/XGBoost → he builds a screening tool → he deploys it on his own organisation where students can actually reach it. A supplementary application reader can click one link and see the whole arc is real. Very few applicants can produce that.
technical_projects.ethics_and_safety_assessment: VERIFIED 2026-08-03 AND HE GOT THIS RIGHT — worth saying explicitly, because handled badly this would have been a liability rather than an asset. A publicly accessible mental-health screening tool aimed at minors is exactly the kind of project that alarms a health-sciences reviewer if the safeguards are missing. Justin's implementation has all of them: (1) CLIENT-SIDE ONLY — the page states twice that 'your answers never leave your browser. No data is collected, stored, or sent anywhere,' which pre-empts the single biggest objection; (2) explicit NON-DIAGNOSTIC disclaimer — 'a screening tool, not a medical diagnosis... should not replace professional evaluation'; (3) CRISIS RESOURCES prominently displayed on both the tool and the README — Kids Help Phone 1-800-668-6868, Crisis Text Line (text HELLO to 686868), and 9-8-8; (4) the survey asks a suicidal-ideation question and pairs it with those crisis lines, which is the responsible way to ask it; (5) proper ATTRIBUTION of the Kaggle dataset and its original creator. This should be mentioned in supplementary applications — the judgement shown here is itself the credential.

gaps_and_next_steps.1_no_performance_metrics: The README reports no accuracy, AUC, precision/recall, confusion matrix or calibration. For a screening tool this is the most conspicuous absence — any technical reader, and any BHSc reviewer who thinks about it for ten seconds, will ask 'how good is it?' and find no answer. He has these numbers from training. Easiest high-value fix available; roughly an hour.
gaps_and_next_steps.2_population_mismatch_IS_THE_GOLD: The model is trained on a Kaggle competition dataset and deployed for Canadian high-school students aged 14-19. Those are not the same population, and the README's limitations text does not name it. This is NOT a flaw to hide — it is the single best supplementary-application material in the entire profile, and it is the same move that made the Harvard answer strong: 'the Roboflow model was trained on 200 images under different lighting and failed in the live demo.' Here the equivalent is: 'I trained on a dataset whose population differs from the students I built this for, and deployed it anyway as a screening aid rather than a diagnostic — here is why that matters, and here is what would fix it: validation against real local student data.' That is a 7/7 answer, and it connects directly to the research-validation pitch he was already advised to make to UofA researchers. ALSO CONFIRM: Kaggle Playground Series datasets are generally described on the competition page as synthetically generated from an original dataset. Justin should check the S4E11 competition page and, if so, state that provenance explicitly — training a deployed tool on synthetic data is a real and interesting limitation to own.
gaps_and_next_steps.3_linkedin_writeup: The remaining A3 piece. Build it around gap 2, not around a feature list. One specific finding that surprised him plus the honest population-mismatch problem, in the style of his Titanic retrospective. This is also the artifact that makes the repo and tool discoverable to anyone who is not already looking for them.
gaps_and_next_steps.4_thin_commit_history: 3 commits on main. Minor, and not worth gaming, but a reader who clicks through sees a thin history. Future work should simply be committed as it happens.

technical_projects.academic_integrity_caution: Publish the TOOL (code, README written fresh in his own framing, demo) — not the assessed IA document itself. Posting the submitted IA write-up publicly while the IB session is still live risks another student copying it and similarity checks flagging both. Confirm the specific rule with Justin's IB coordinator; default to withholding the document until results are released. This does not restrict publishing the codebase or a newly written project README.
